- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is trending upward, lower the forecast by 3–7% to reflect bearish sentiment bias.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true values by >5% in early days of the 30d horizon, apply a 2–5% downward correction to the first 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment shows a sudden shift from negative to positive (e.g., +0.3 to +0.7), delay the forecast peak by 1–3 days and reduce magnitude by 5–10%.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60–65) and forecast is above 65, reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days.  
- For sentiment history with low volatility (±0.15), forecast should be closer to historical mean; if forecast deviates >3% from 30d average, adjust toward mean.  
- If forecast shows a sharp downward spike after a positive sentiment peak, reduce the spike by 10–20% to avoid sentiment-driven overcorrection.
